title: Fried Sage and Cannabis Gnocchi in Brown Butter
h1: Crispy Sage Gnocchi with Cannabis Brown Butter
metaDescription: A 30-minute cannabis gnocchi dinner with crisp fried sage and brown butter, finished with cannabutter over low heat at the end for a more even dose.
excerpt: Store-bought gnocchi, crisp sage and brown butter, with the cannabutter stirred in at the very end over low heat, or a measured canna-oil drizzle per plate.
keyTakeaways: Brown the plain butter first, then lower the heat before the cannabutter goes in. Never brown the cannabutter itself.
For the most exact dose, skip infused butter and drizzle measured canna-oil over each plate.
With refrigerated gnocchi, dinner takes about 30 minutes.
Fan leaves add flavor, not a dependable dose: they carry far fewer cannabinoids than flower, mostly as THCA.
body:
This cannabis gnocchi is an easy cannabis dinner that takes about 30 minutes: store-bought potato gnocchi tossed in sage brown butter and topped with crisp fried sage. The dose goes in at the finish, after the browning is done. Melt cannabutter into the sauce over low heat, or drizzle measured canna-oil on each plate.

## Why the cannabutter goes in last

Browning butter takes real heat, and THC doesn't benefit from it. In lab studies of heated cannabis extracts, THC levels fell as heating ran hotter or longer, possibly through evaporation, and at the highest temperatures some turned into CBN. So the plain butter does the browning. Once it smells nutty, turn the heat to low, let the pan settle, and stir in the [cannabutter](/blog/canna-butter-recipe/) just until it melts. A drizzle of [canna-oil](/blog/canna-oil-recipe/) on each plate is even more exact.

Either way, divide the THC you add by the number of plates, and toss well so the sauce coats evenly. Our [THC dosage guide](/blog/thc-dosage-guide/) helps you choose an amount.

## What you need for cannabis gnocchi

Refrigerated or shelf-stable potato gnocchi, olive oil, a big bunch of fresh sage, plain butter, your measured cannabutter, parmesan, salt, pepper and a pinch of chili flakes. Starting a fresh batch of cannabutter? Browse your nearest High Society store's [menu](/shop/) for flower and order ahead for in-store or curbside pickup.

If you grow cannabis legally at home, a few dry fan leaves can fry alongside the sage for flavor. In Michigan, adults 21+ may grow up to 12 plants per household, out of public view and behind a lock. Raw leaves are mostly THCA, the non-intoxicating form explained in our [THC vs. THCA guide](/blog/thc-vs-thca/), but frying can turn some of it into THC. Think of them as a garnish, not a dose you can count on, and tell guests they're there.

## The order of operations

Start the pasta water first. While it heats, fry the sage leaves in olive oil until crisp. Boil the gnocchi until they float, brown the plain butter, lower the heat, then add the cannabutter and chopped sage. Toss in the gnocchi with parmesan, plate evenly and top with the fried leaves.

## Swaps

- **Gluten-free:** gluten-free gnocchi work the same way; toss them gently.
- **Canna-oil only:** brown plain butter, skip the cannabutter, and drizzle measured canna-oil over each plate.
- **Crunch:** toasted walnuts, hazelnuts or pine nuts.
- **Another sauce:** our [super green canna pesto](/blog/super-green-canna-pesto/) makes a quick, herby finish.

## Storage and labeling

Eat the gnocchi right out of the pan, since they turn dense as they sit. Refrigerate any leftovers within two hours in a container labeled with the dose and date, and finish them within 3 to 4 days. Keep infused food away from children and pets, and if someone eats it by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222.

21+ only. Please consume responsibly.

faq.q: Do fresh cannabis leaves get you high?
faq.a: Not the way flower does. In one lab profile, leaves held about 1 to 2% cannabinoids against roughly 16 to 20% in flowers. Raw plant material is also mostly THCA, and how much of it a quick fry turns into THC is hard to predict. So a few fried leaves are a garnish that may add a small, variable amount of THC. Tell guests they're there.

Yes, and it's the most precise option. Make the dish with plain butter only, plate it, then drizzle a measured amount of canna-oil over each serving. Everyone gets the same dose, and anyone who'd like a plain plate simply skips the drizzle. A fruity olive oil infusion suits sage and parmesan.

faq.q: Can I make the gnocchi from scratch?
faq.a: Absolutely. Bake russet potatoes, rice them while hot, then work in flour, an egg and salt just until a soft dough forms. Roll it into ropes, cut 1-inch pieces and boil them until they float. Homemade gnocchi are plain, so the dosing steps stay exactly the same.

ingredients: 1 pound refrigerated or shelf-stable potato gnocchi
20 to 24 fresh sage leaves, plus 1 tablespoon chopped sage
Cannabutter, measured for 4 servings (see the dosing note)
Salt, black pepper and a pinch of chili flakes
Optional: a few dry fan leaves from a legal home grow
steps: Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil.

Heat the oil in a wide pan set over medium-high. Fry the whole sage leaves, and any fan leaves, in small batches for 20 to 30 seconds until crisp. Drain on paper towels and pour off all but a thin film of oil.
Drop the gnocchi into the boiling water and cook until they bob to the surface, 2 to 3 minutes. Scoop them out, saving 1/2 cup of the water.
Add the plain butter to the pan over medium heat and swirl until it foams, turns golden brown and smells nutty, 2 to 3 minutes.
Turn the heat to low and wait 30 seconds. Stir in the cannabutter and chopped sage just until melted.
Add the gnocchi and parmesan and toss until glossy, loosening with splashes of the saved water. Season, divide evenly among 4 plates and crown with the fried sage.
recipe.dosingNote: **Per-plate estimate:** total THC in the cannabutter ÷ 4 plates. Example: 1 tablespoon of cannabutter that works out to about 20 mg THC gives roughly 5 mg per plate, if you toss well and portion evenly. A homemade batch's strength depends on the potency of your flower and on decarboxylation and infusion losses, so the figure is an estimate. For the canna-oil version, measure the drizzle per plate instead. Start low, wait at least 2 hours before seconds, label leftovers, and keep infused food away from children and pets.

sources.label: Wang M. et al. (2016), Decarboxylation study of acidic cannabinoids, Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research
Jin D. et al. (2020), Secondary metabolites profiled in cannabis inflorescences, leaves, stem barks and roots, Scientific Reports
Moreno-Sanz G. (2016), Critical review of tetrahydrocannabinolic acid A (THCA-A), Cannabis and Cannabinoid Research
Michigan Judicial Institute: Controlled Substances Benchbook, sec. 8.14, Scope of the MRTMA
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: Cannabis frequently asked questions
University of Illinois Extension: Leftovers (food safety)

review.summary: 19 claims checked: 15 ok, 1 wrong, 3 overstated (4 fixed). Leaf and heat claims now match what the cited studies show; the home-grow line matches law-facts.

claims.claim: In lab studies of heated extracts, THC fell as heating ran hotter or longer, 'through evaporation and oxidation'
claims.fix: now 'possibly through evaporation, and at the highest temperatures some turned into CBN', matching what the reviewed studies observed
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/ (Wang 2016, full text via Europe PMC REST), reviewing earlier work: loss at longer times at 145°C 'possibly due to evaporation of Δ9-THC'; 'formation of an oxidation product, CBN, was observed at 160°C and 180°C'

claims.claim: Browning butter takes real heat, so the plain butter browns and the cannabutter goes in after the heat is lowered
claims.source: reasoning from the same Wang 2016 review (losses rise with temperature); brief mustAvoid (never brown the cannabutter)

claims.claim: A measured canna-oil drizzle per plate is even more exact than infused butter tossed through the pan
claims.source: reasoning: a per-plate measure removes the uneven-coating step; no figure

claims.claim: Dose per plate = total THC ÷ plates; example about 20 mg in 1 tablespoon ÷ 4 = roughly 5 mg
claims.source: arithmetic (20 ÷ 4 = 5); example potency, not a fixed figure

claims.claim: A homemade batch's strength depends on flower potency and decarboxylation and infusion losses
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549281/: 'the conversion of the acid to Δ9-THC was never perfectly complete without loss or degradation of starting material'

claims.claim: In Michigan, adults 21+ may grow up to 12 plants per household, out of public view and behind a lock
claims.source: facts/law-facts.json mi-au-home-grow: 'An adult may grow up to 12 plants for personal use at home, with no more than 12 plants on the premises at once, kept out of public view and behind a lock.' (MJI benchbook sec. 8.14, in the sources list)

claims.claim: In one lab profile, leaves held about 1 to 2% cannabinoids against roughly 16 to 20% in flowers
claims.source: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7039888/ (Jin 2020, Sci Rep, abstract via E-utilities, PMID 32094454): inflorescence 'cannabinoids (15.77-20.37%)'; leaf 'cannabinoids (1.10-2.10%)' (three chemovars)

claims.claim: Raw leaves are mostly THCA, the non-intoxicating form
claims.source: Jin 2020 full text (NCBI PMC efetch): THC-dominant chemovars had 'THCA as the dominant compound ... in both leaf and inflorescence tissue'; 'Cannabinoids mainly exist in the plant as carboxylic acids'; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5549534/ (Moreno-Sanz 2016, abstract via E-utilities, PMID 28861488): 'Contrary to THC, THCA-A does not elicit psychoactive effects in humans'

claims.claim: THCA 'needs sustained heat to become THC', so leaves 'fried for seconds' are only a garnish
claims.fix: FAQ now says how much a quick fry converts is hard to predict and fried leaves may add a small, variable amount of THC; the body adds that frying can turn some THCA into THC and to tell guests
claims.source: Moreno-Sanz 2016 abstract: 'Decarboxylation also occurs rapidly during baking of edibles, smoking, or vaporizing'; Wang 2016: decarboxylation rate constants climb steeply with temperature (80 to 110 °C tested), while frying oil runs far hotter

claims.claim: Takeaway: 'Fresh cannabis leaves add flavor' (the recipe and body call for dry fan leaves)
claims.fix: now 'Fan leaves add flavor', matching the ingredient list ('a few dry fan leaves from a legal home grow')
claims.source: internal consistency with recipe.ingredients and the body

claims.claim: With refrigerated gnocchi, dinner takes about 30 minutes
Fry sage 20 to 30 seconds; gnocchi float in 2 to 3 minutes; butter browns and smells nutty in 2 to 3 minutes
claims.source: ordinary stovetop timings with visual cues given; no safety figure

claims.claim: Gnocchi turn dense as they sit; refrigerate leftovers within two hours and finish within 3 to 4 days
claims.source: https://extension.illinois.edu/food-safety/leftovers (WebFetch): 'Leftover food should be refrigerated or frozen within two hours of serving.'; 'Use refrigerated leftover food within 3-4 days'

claims.claim: If someone eats it by accident, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html (WebFetch): 'call a poison control center at: at 1-800-222-1222.'

claims.claim: Start low and wait at least 2 hours before seconds; label leftovers; keep from children and pets
claims.source: https://www.cdc.gov/cannabis/faq/index.html: 'it can take up to 2 hours to feel the effects from the drug.'; 'Infants or young children who unintentionally ingest cannabis are more likely to require hospital admission'

claims.claim: Homemade gnocchi: bake and rice russets, work in flour, egg and salt, cut 1-inch pieces, boil until they float
claims.source: standard potato gnocchi method; no figure beyond piece size

claims.claim: High Society: browse your nearest store's menu for flower and order ahead for in-store or curbside pickup; the fan-leaf paragraph carries no High Society mention
claims.source: facts/hs-facts.json services.ordering, services.inStorePickup, services.curbside, services.productCategories (flower); nothing implies High Society sells leaves (brief mustAvoid)

claims.claim: Meta description: cannabutter at the end 'for an accurate dose'
claims.fix: now 'for a more even dose': adding it last improves the spread, but a homemade figure stays an estimate (dosing note)

review.notes: Independent fact-check, 2026-10-24. Jin 2020 read in full (NCBI PMC efetch) and Moreno-Sanz 2016 and Wang 2016 rechecked; the fan-leaf copy no longer implies that a quick fry leaves THCA unconverted, since the reviewed evidence says decarboxylation is fast at high heat and no study measured fried leaves. The home-grow sentence matches law-facts mi-au-home-grow. Sources list kept (all five https and supportive); Moreno-Sanz 2016 added to the sources list for the THCA lines. Writer's notes: Cannabutter is never browned (brief mustAvoid). Fan-leaf paragraph carries no shop or High Society mention, so nothing implies High Society sells leaves. High Society mentioned once (menu for flower, pickup).
writerClaims: THC falls with hotter/longer heating, partly via oxidation to CBN; THCA is the predominant form in the plant: Wang 2016 (abstract and full-text introduction).
Leaves about 1.10-2.10% cannabinoids vs inflorescences 15.77-20.37%: Jin 2020 abstract (three chemovars).
Home grow: up to 12 plants per household, not visible from a public place, locked: law-facts mi-au-home-grow, MJI Controlled Substances Benchbook sec. 8.14.
Poison Control 1-800-222-1222: CDC cannabis FAQ. Leftovers: refrigerate within two hours, 3-4 days: University of Illinois Extension.
